column1: # `zig build check-portable`'s known-failure baseline for wasm32 (wasm32-wasi,
# 32-bit pointers/usize — see build.zig's check-portable comment for why wasi
# and not freestanding: freestanding fails to compile the default TEST RUNNER
# itself, before any module code is reached at all, because it reaches for
# `std.Io.Threaded`'s RNG seed / argv / stdin, none of which freestanding has).
# One row per `platform = .any` module whose test binary currently fails to
# COMPILE for wasm32. Two DIFFERENT things land in this file and the reason
#   - a genuine 32-bit pointer/integer-width defect (a `u64`/`u47` narrowed to
#     `usize`, a shift amount too wide for a 32-bit `usize`, a 64-bit atomic,
#     a comptime literal or eval-quota that only overflows at 32 bits) — this
#     is the class `check-portable` exists to catch, and would very plausibly
#     also fail on a REAL 32-bit OS target (mips-linux-musleabihf, arm32, ...).
#   - a `[wasi-surface]` gap — the module reaches something WASI specifically
#     does not implement (no real threads by default, libc not auto-linked,
#     reached by a module that is Linux-coded despite claiming `platform =
#     wasi). These are believed target-surface artifacts of picking wasi as
#     the OS half of the 32-bit probe, not bitness bugs — a real 32-bit-linux
#     target has real threads and auto-linked libc. UNVERIFIED against a real
#     32-bit OS target as of this file's creation; a `[wasi-surface]` tag is
#     a hypothesis about WHY, not a promise that fixing wasi would leave the
# Format: <module><TAB><reason>, one line per module. `#`-comment and blank
# lines are ignored. The reason is copied from the actual `zig build
# portable-<module>` compiler error -- never invented, never a generic
# restatement that could be pasted onto any row. Local toolchain install
# paths are stripped down to the `std/...`-relative path (no `/home/<user>/`
# THIS LIST IS A BASELINE, NOT A SUPPRESSION. `check-portable`
# (`PortableBaselineStep` in build.zig) fails the build in BOTH directions:
#   - a module NOT listed here that fails to compile for wasm32 -- a new or
#   - a module LISTED here that now PASSES -- a stale entry, which must be
#     deleted, not left for "in case it comes back". A baseline that can only
#     grow is a list nobody re-reads, which is exactly the shape this repo has
#     enforce the identical rule for the identical reason).
# Fixing a module's 32-bit bug does not require asking permission to shrink
# this file -- the gate REQUIRES the row gone the moment the module passes.
# ── Root-cause groups, measured 2026-08-18, zig 0.16.0, wasm32-wasi, ReleaseSmall
#    against the module_list in build.zig at this commit (195 platform=.any
# CASCADES from ONE shared bug (not independent defects):
#     (http itself + everything that imports it: acme, cookies, cors, grpc,
#     health, idempotency, jwt, mcp-http, openapi, ratelimit, requestid,
#     router, security-headers, sessions, staticfiles, tracecontext, validate,
#     webhooksig). NOTE: most of these 19 ALSO carry an independent
#     [wasi-surface] thread-spawn/libc finding of their own (their live-server
#     tests spawn a real thread) -- fixing Server.zig:2696 alone will not turn
#     all 19 green under wasm32-wasi, only under a target with real threads.
# Independent 32-bit pointer/integer-width defects (own bug, not cascaded):
#   shift-width (u6 shift amount, target wants u5)          —  5 modules
#     (same class as the original `qr` BitWriter bug this gate was built for)
#   comptime literal too big for 32-bit usize/u5             —  7 modules
#   comptime eval-quota exceeded (bignum limb count grows
#   64-bit atomic RMW unsupported at wasm32 baseline         —  7 modules
#     (UNVERIFIED whether this reproduces on real mips-linux, where 64-bit
#     atomics are commonly available via libatomic; may be wasm-specific)
#   libc not auto-linked (extern "c" fn reached)               — 36 modules
#   std.process.Environ has no `.view` on wasi (testkit's own
#     env-var helper, pulled in via test_deps)                 — 28 modules
#   std.os.linux reached on a non-Linux target (module claims
#     platform=.any but its code is Linux-only)                — 19 modules
#   downstream void-type struct-init (follows from the above)  —  4 modules
#   std.posix hard `@compileError("unsupported OS")` for wasi   —  2 modules
#   module's own comptime gate declares itself Linux-only
#   std.posix wait-status API is void on wasi (procrun)         —  1 module
